chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Salamah, Abu Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, that Ali (peace be upon him) said:
The Jews and the Christians do not slaughter your sacrifices, and none should slaughter them except the Muslim.
ai.seo_question: Are Jewish and Christian sacrifices considered valid in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the Shia juristic position that the ritual slaughter of Jews and Christians is invalid for general consumption, distinguishing it from the broader Sunni view of *Ahl al-Kitab*. This ruling underscores the necessity of specific Islamic criteria for *dhabihah*, emphasizing that mere monotheism is insufficient without adherence to Islamic ritual law. It serves as a foundational text in Shia fiqh for determining the permissibility of meat from People of the Book in contemporary contexts.
